tier_reason: Paper Table 3 compares ctbignum against GMP mpn_mul (and NTL) with Apple LLVM 9.0.0 -O3 -march=native, forced inlining, on a stated Kaby Lake i5 2.3 GHz; the benchmark code is public at benchmarks/src/bench-mul.cpp (mul_cbn vs mul_gmp vs mul_ntl, Google Benchmark).

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Apple LLVM 9.0.0, -O3 -march=native with forced inlining of mul (Table 3); Table 1 uses -O3 without -march=native
corrections.claimed_speedup: Table 3 (-march=native, forced inlining): 2 limbs 4 ns vs GMP mpn_mul 14 ns (3.5x); 4 limbs 18 vs 29 ns (1.6x); 8 limbs 85 vs 67 ns (GMP 1.27x faster). Table 1 (-O3 only): 2 limbs 5 vs 13 ns, 4 limbs 19 vs 30 ns, 8 limbs 125 vs 69 ns. GMP wins from 5-6 limbs up (ratios derived from page data)
corrections.caveats: Win is only for small fixed widths (2-4/5 limbs); GMP is faster from about 5-6 limbs and up to 1.8x faster at 8 limbs without -march=native; the headline numbers need -march=native plus forced inlining; 2018 paper on 2017 hardware; bench needs GMP, NTL, libff and Google Benchmark; not all functions are constant-time.

notes: Numbers match Table 3 of the paper, but the record left out that they need -march=native plus forced inlining. I fixed the flags and noted the crossover point, where GMP becomes faster.

tier_reason: arXiv 2410.18129 compares against GMP 6.2.0 (mpn_sec_powm) and OpenSSL 3.2.1 with GCC 9.4.0 -O3 -funroll-all-loops -march=native on an i7-1165G7 (Turbo off); the paper links the public code repo (Montgomery/, WindowExponentiation/, Openssl_RSA_Z_512/ dirs).

corrections.claimed_speedup: 8 batched Montgomery multiplications vs 8 GMP calls: 5.34x (1024-bit), 4.86x (2048), 3.95x (4096); vs OpenSSL 4.31x/4.10x/3.69x. Batched fixed-window modexp vs GMP mpn_sec_powm: 5.42x/5.17x/4.66x; vs OpenSSL BN_mod_exp_mont_consttime 3.98x/3.71x/3.30x; vs OpenSSL BN_mod_exp_mont_consttimex2 (AVX512-IFMA 256-bit) only 1.75x (1024) / 1.38x (2048)
corrections.caveats: Batch-of-8 SIMD throughput compared with 8 sequential GMP/OpenSSL calls; needs AVX512-IFMA (VPMADD52); only modular multiplication and exponentiation, not general bigint; against OpenSSL's own IFMA path (consttimex2) the gain shrinks to 1.38-1.75x; research code (7 commits, 3 stars), GPL-3.0.

notes: The record's claimed speedup put the multiplication-vs-OpenSSL range next to the exponentiation figures. I corrected it and added the much smaller margin over OpenSSL's IFMA path.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed paper (ARITH 2019, arXiv 1901.04289) Table I compares Arb's dot product with MPFR mul/add, fma and sum on an Intel i5-4300U; compiler and flags are not stated, so it cannot be A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Paper: 'A factor 1.5 to 2.0 speedup persists up to several hundred bits'; up to 128 bits 3-4x faster. Table I cycles/term, arb dot vs MPFR fma: 53 bits 40 vs 99, 106 bits 49 vs 156, 212 bits 133 vs 208, 848 bits 522 vs 619; vs MPFR mul/add: 40 vs 74, 49 vs 97, 133 vs 237, 522 vs 670

notes: The numbers match the MPFR fma column. The repo is archived (last commit 2023-11-15) because Arb was merged into FLINT. If FLINT (flintlib/flint, also in wave 8) passes verification, consider marking this entry duplicate of FLINT.
